data.gender_notes: Ishant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ishant is a compound name derived from two words: 'Ish' and 'An'. Ish means God, while An means protection. Thus, Ishant means 'God of Protection'. The name Ishant carries the meaning “God of Protection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Ishant usually hope their child will grow to embody god of protection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ishant is a powerful name associated with the Hindu god Shiva, who is the god of destruction and protection. The name Ishant signifies strength, power, and protection from all harms.
data.etymology: Ishant belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Protection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ishant total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

The name resonates deeply with both the optimistic and the fearful, offering a reassuring sense of security, and represents the benevolent aspect of Hindu gods who protect their devotees. Furthermore, the name Ishant is also used as a personal name for boys, making it a popular choice in Hindu communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ishant holds immense significance in Hindu philosophy, as it is a reminder of the timeless divine protection that God provides. Ishant is an eternal reminder that even in the darkest of times, amidst trials and tribulations, one can always find solace and refuge in the loving embrace of God. It shows us that even when we live in challenging circumstances, we should never forget the presence of our divine protectors. This name can act as a constant motivation to seek refuge, comfort, and strength in the divine. In simple terms, the name Ishant means "Protector of the Divine," it connects one's spiritual self to the divine and provides a sense of peace and security during difficult times.

historical_references.reference: Ishant is a name of Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction. He is also known as Ishana, Rudra, and Mahadeva. Ishant is often depicted with multiple arms, each holding various weapons, and a third eye on his forehead. He is the supreme lord, the ultimate reality, and the creator, destroyer, and preserver of the universe.

The name Ishant is also mentioned in Mahabharata, the great Indian epic. In this text, Ishant is the name of a celestial being who is a messenger of Shiva. He is sent to the battlefield of Kurukshetra to help the Pandava prince Bhima in his fight against the Kaurava prince Duryodhana.
